newsitem.title: UK: Palm oil bubble bursts on European veg oil market.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil bubble bursts on European veg oil market.

text.p: European traders said on Thursday that the bubble seems to have finally burst for palm oil with prices dropping by as much as $10 a tonne on the local market at midday.
"We have had rumours and all sorts in recent weeks as speculators have tried their best to hold the market up, but in the end fundamentals appear to have won," said one trader.

The market started to look vulnerable when reports of a quicker pickup in palm oil output than expected after the long holiday in Malaysia started to circulate in the market against a background of slow exports.
In his last report Malaysian private forecaster Ivan Wong projected a fall of 21 percent in Malaysian output during February, but now traders are looking for a figure below 20 percent.
Wong's next report is likely to be released on Friday.
The future trend of palm oil depends to some extent on what happens in Chicago later on Thusrday. But here, too, some European traders say they feel the party may be over.

"Chicago was looking overdone with funds pushing it even higher, but it fell overnight and again this morning in Project A trading, so may be some sense is returning to the market as a whole," said another trader.
Traders have been saying for some time that palm oil is over priced against soft oils and only a run of very high prices in Chicago could stop it falling.
At midday in Europe crude palm oil was $5 to $10 down after Apr traded at $555 a tonne cif.
Products were unchanged to $6 lower after Mar RBD oil traded at $551, while $581.50 and $580 was paid for the same positions in olein.
Apr olein traded at $574 and $572.50 while $566, $565 and $560 a tonne fob Malaysian ports was paid for May/Jun.
Coconut oil and palmkernel oil sellers were $2.50 lower.
In soft oils soy oil was one guilder down while rape oil was 0.75 to one guilders lower.
